source.title: Scaling sparse feature circuit finding for in-context learning
source.authors: Dmitrii Kharlapenko; Stepan Shabalin; Fazl Barez; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAE feature recovery and causal interventions in language models, rather than the original toy-network setup, to test whether interpretable sparse features can be recovered and have causal effects. It also reports a limited finding about cases where detector information is split across features.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and discusses SAE features, but does not test superposition geometry, feature sparsity or importance, capacity competition, or feature dimensionality. Its own SAE recovery and intervention results bear on V4; its reported detector-feature splitting bears partly on V5. Hyperparameter and layer choices are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs and transcoders as tools to analyse in-context learning in Gemma 1 2B, with some Gemma 2 and Phi-3 runs. Its results are about the ICL mechanism (task-execution and task-detection features, circuit faithfulness, steering specificity) and about how well its own methods (TVC, adapted SFC) perform. It does not test whether superposition exists, whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. Superposition is mentioned only in related work, citing Elhage et al. 2022.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that SAEs are valuable circuit-analysis tools for ICL. They identify task-execution and task-detection features with causal effects and decompose task vectors with TVC. Limitations are that the work is restricted to the simple task-vector setting and the circuit analysis is centred on Gemma 1 2B.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method. It trains and applies SAEs and transcoders, cleans task-vector decompositions, and uses feature steering and circuit ablations to study ICL.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected layer varies by analysis (layer 12 for task execution and layer 11 for task detection); steering scales and SAE configurations vary, and the paper notes that Gemma 2 2B does not have one common optimal steering scale. The circuit search is constrained to intermediate layers 10-17, with the main analysis focused on layers 10-15.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma 1 2B, SAE latents selected by task-vector cleaning are interpretable and causally steer specific ICL tasks, with spillover among related tasks (Figs 6, 10, 22, 25).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task vectors for ICL decompose into a few task-specific SAE latents that causally induce zero-shot task behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: For some tasks, detector information was split across several token-level SAE features rather than forming one feature. The authors attribute this to limited SAE expressivity (Appendix I).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a task maps to a single SAE feature depends on SAE capacity and width.

fits_no_version.finding: An adapted SFC on Gemma 1 2B reaches average faithfulness 0.6 with 500 nodes. Detector ablation reduces activation of the matching executor features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse feature circuits for ICL link task-detection features to task-execution features.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The main circuit analysis is centered on Gemma 1 2B and a simple task-vector subset of ICL. Some detector-execution connections are weak, and the authors report detector features split across token-level features for some tasks. Exact values for several steering and ablation results are only in figures.

untested.parts: No toy models, overlap geometry or sparsity-dependent transitions.
No test of capacity competition or feature importance.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
SAEs are used as a tool. There is no measurement of how features are distributed across neurons and no test of whether real models are in superposition.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds or widths, or canonicality of SAE features. There is only an anecdotal mention of detector information split across token-level features.
No comparison of one-dimensional and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's guess of 'tests/T2' is overturned. The paper's results concern ICL mechanisms and the performance of its own methods, built on SAEs used as an instrument. No row measures what any superposition version names, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The study does not test whether polysemanticity arises from limited capacity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
The study does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

It tests SAE-recoverable features in several LLMs, including some causal effects, but does not measure how widely features are distributed across neurons or establish that the findings generalize to LLMs broadly.
The study reports some task-detection features split across several token-level features, but does not test feature stability across settings or whether SAE features are canonical units in general.
The study uses SAE latent vectors but does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

relation.reason: Sparse dictionary features serve as tools for identifying and intervening on task-detection and task-execution mechanisms; the study does not independently evaluate superposition or dictionary completeness, stability, or canonicality.

tranche.reason: The study uses SAEs and transcoders to investigate ICL circuits and evaluates its TVC and SFC methods. The reported results do not directly test a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: All ten rows describe ICL mechanisms or the study's analysis methods; their cannot_determine states and lack of claim-version links are appropriate. Appendix I attributes fragmented detector features to limited SAE expressivity without testing dictionary canonicality or stability.
